note: Re-read 2026-10-30 (independent judge) after commit 60e9406387 changed only comments in these units (RFC6810 tags removed, VALIDATES prose rewritten; no assertion line changed). RFC 8210 Section 5 reads 'Reserved fields (marked "zero" in PDU diagrams) MUST be zero on transmission and MUST be ignored on receipt.' Transmit: TestWriteResetQueryZeroesReservedOverGarbage writes a Reset Query over a 0xFF buffer and asserts octets 2-3 are zero, the specified fields are real and octet 8 is untouched, so a writer that inherits residue goes red (TestWriteResetQuery alone writes over a zero buffer and could not); TestWriteSerialQuery is the negative, octets 2-3 of a Serial Query carry the Session ID 0x1234 and are not zeroed. writeResetQuery takes the version as a parameter and zeroes regardless of it, so the rtrVersionMax buffers prove the same write a version 1 session makes. Receipt: TestReservedPrefixFieldsPreserveValidation runs a version 1 session whose IPv4 and IPv6 Prefix PDUs carry 0xFF in every reserved octet and asserts the route validates Valid; TestRTRReservedOctetsIgnoredOnReceipt sends a Cache Reset with 0xFFFF in its reserved octets 2-3 over TCP and asserts the sync still ends with errRtrCacheResetReceivedWillDo and serial 0, while its negative shows the same 0xFFFF in a Cache Response is adopted as the Session ID, so the receiver ignores only reserved fields. Both clauses and both polarities hold.
